problem:
The **exact** value of $c$ such that the average value of $f(x)=-15\sqrt{x}+6$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $-4$ is

$c=$
{{field-1}}.

feedback.worked_solution:
To solve for $c,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}\,{\int }_{a}^{b}h(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 2 & =\frac{1}{c-0}\,{\int }_{0}^{c}(4x-6)\,\text{d}x \\ 2 & =\frac{1}{c}(2{x}^{2}-6x){|}_{0}^{c} \\ 2 & =\frac{1}{c}[(2{c}^{2}-6c)-0] \\ 2 & =2c-6 \\ 8 & =2c \\ c & =4\end{aligned}
$$
